Well, so there's two ways that this can help. The first is just to lower your monthly bill. If you apply for energy assistance and you qualify, then what happens is that the bill you get from your power company is actually reduced. And you can look right there on the bill and say, oh, this is by how much it's reduced every month. And it can be up to $1,400 over the course of a year in reduced bills for your electricity. So that's one thing. But the other way that this can help is you can apply to repair a furnace or make other emergency repairs that you might have. Here's an example of what that meant for somebody in Minnesota. This is a story a man told me that he had lived in his home for 30 years and he was living on a fixed income. He had a living with disability and suddenly his furnace went out. There was no way that he could afford to repair his furnace. But thanks to energy assistance, he was able to get help with that and that allowed him to stay in his home. So that's kind of two examples of how this can be so helpful.
